---
title: Quickstart
description: Receive your first test email in under five minutes. You need an API key from the dashboard and a project that sends email.
sidebarTitle: Quickstart
---

<Callout type="note" title="Before you start">
Create an API key in the dashboard and export it as `TESTINBOX_API_KEY`. Sandbox and production keys are separate; see [Authentication](./authentication#api-keys).
</Callout>

<Steps>
<Step title="Create an inbox">
Every test gets its own address. A short `ttl` keeps the sandbox clean; the inbox is deleted when it expires.

```typescript title="signup.test.ts"
const inbox = await client.inboxes.create({ ttl: 600 });
```

Returns an [Inbox](/api/inboxes/create-inbox#response-201) with `address` and `expiresAt`.
</Step>
<Step title="Trigger your application">
Use the inbox address wherever your application would send email: a sign-up form, a password reset, an invoice.

```typescript
await app.signUp({ email: inbox.address });
```
</Step>
<Step title="Wait for an email">
`wait()` blocks until a message matching your criteria arrives or the timeout passes. Match by subject, sender, or body.

```typescript
const message = await inbox.messages.wait({ subject: /verify/i, timeout: 30_000 });
```
</Step>
<Step title="Assert its contents">
```typescript
expect(message.links[0]).toContain("/verify?token=");
```
</Step>
</Steps>

## Choose your client

<Tabs>
<Tab label="TypeScript">
```typescript
import { TestInbox } from "@testinbox/client";

const client = new TestInbox({ apiKey: process.env.TESTINBOX_API_KEY });
```
</Tab>
<Tab label="Python">
```python
from testinbox import TestInbox

client = TestInbox(api_key=os.environ["TESTINBOX_API_KEY"])
```
</Tab>
<Tab label="cURL">
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.testinbox.email/v1/inboxes \
  -H "X-Api-Key: $TESTINBOX_API_KEY" \
  -d '{"ttl": 600}'
```
</Tab>
</Tabs>
